interest: Contrasts 1931 Inouye's tight-money gold defense with 1936 Baba's rate cuts to absorb deficit bonds after the gold standard's fall.
overview: File 894.5161 (1931-36): a November 1931 despatch reports the Bank of Japan sharply raised discount rates under Hijikata and Inouye to defend the gold standard; a May 1936 despatch reports Baba's Bank of Japan cut rates to stimulate bond demand and convert 5% bonds to 3.5%, abandoning Takahashi's tapering policy.

people.name: Hisaakira Hijikata
people.role: Governor of the Bank of Japan

people.name: Korekiyo Takahashi
people.role: Former Minister of Finance (referenced in relation to the 'Takahashi policy')

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet and attached extract from Despatch No. 379 reporting the Bank of Japan's increase of its official discount and loan rates in October 1931 to defend the gold standard.
subfiles.summary: October 1931: the Bank of Japan raised its discount and loan rates to curb gold outflows; Governor Hijikata and Finance Minister Inouye insisted the hike, despite business criticism, would not destabilize finance and was essential to defend the gold standard.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 379 (Cross-Reference Sheet and Attached Copy) from Forbes on Bank of Japan Discount Rate Increase

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet and attached report extract from Despatch No. 1829 detailing the lowering of interest and discount rates by the Bank of Japan and semi-official banks in April 1936 to support government bond issues.
subfiles.summary: April 1936: the Bank of Japan and semi-official banks cut rates 0.37% to make bonds more attractive than deposits, enabling conversion of 5% bonds to 3.5% and abandoning Takahashi's tapering policy, with Baba also planning a tax readjustment by October.
